description: Checkpoint bodies, origins, the anchor log and record anchor artifacts (Anchor §4 to §6, §10.3, §10.6 and §10.7). A verifier must read every body in bodies.valid back to its origin, size and root and hash it to checkpointDigest; refuse every body in bodies.invalid and bodies.nonString (each invalid body also records what C2SP and the stock Go parser make of it: c2spConforming and stockParserAccepts); map every chainSegments entry both ways and refuse every invalid one; give every domain case its result; reproduce the anchor log of anchorLog; and give every artifact case the anchorValid, reason, merkleProofValid, p, anchorPosition and anchorNamespace in its expect, and report exactly the checks it lists (Anchor §10.7: ids, outcomes, reasons and facts, in order). No case carries an EVM raw transaction or an RFC 3161 token, so no publication can be true.
source: Computed by scripts/generate-checkpoint-vectors.mjs, which imports nothing but node:crypto and transcribes C2SP tlog-checkpoint and signed-note v1.0.0, transparency-dev/formats log.Checkpoint.Unmarshal at v0.1.1 (with Go's strconv.ParseUint and base64.StdEncoding), RFC 4648 §4 base64, RFC 3629 UTF-8, RFC 6962 §2.1 MTH and §2.1.1 PATH (recursive), RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2 and Anchor §4, §5, §6, §8.1, §10.3, §10.6 and §10.7 by hand. Every valid case was read back, every invalid case refused, and every artifact case given its stated outcome and checks by the script's own transcription of §10.3, §10.6 and §10.7 before being written. The SDK implementation (src/attestation/checkpoint.ts, src/attestation/anchor-verify.ts) uses Buffer base64, TextDecoder and the engine's iterative Merkle code. scripts/regenerate-vectors.ts does not and must not rewrite this file.

format.body:
<origin>
<size, ASCII decimal, no leading zero, 1 to 2^53 - 1>
<root: canonical padded RFC 4648 §4 base64 of 32 bytes>
. LF only, a final newline, no extension lines. The origin is printable ASCII (0x21-0x7E) with no "+".
format.checkpointDigest: SHA-256 of the body bytes, lowercase hex. An anchor-log leaf; for the anchor log's own checkpoint, P.
format.origins: <ns>/<id>/anchors; <ns>/<id>/evidence/<lowercase hex of the chain id's UTF-8 bytes>; <ns>/<id>/<one other segment> (an SDK source-log kind, or a platform opaque id). No empty segment. "evidence" alone is not a log.
format.domainRule: The anchor origin is <prefix>/anchors with a two-segment prefix; the log origin is a non-anchor origin under the same prefix. With a chain id supplied, the log must be that chain's evidence log: an evidence log's chain segment spells the chain id (string equality), and a source log of any other kind is chain_id_mismatch, except under the platform's namespaces, exactly "log.tzun.ai" and "test.log.tzun.ai" (tzun-anchor/1 §4.3.3 and §4.3.4: a platform deployment that anchors for testing uses the namespace test.log.tzun.ai, so its domain prefix is test.log.tzun.ai/<deploymentId>, §4.3.1), whose source-log origins are opaque and leave the chain unchecked. A name that extends either is not the platform's. With no chain id, the chain is unchecked. A namespace beginning "test." is a test origin.
format.anchorLog: Per epoch, every member checkpoint's digest is appended in ascending bytewise origin order; the anchor checkpoint is taken at the new size and P = SHA-256(anchor checkpoint body).
format.artifactExpect: expect.reason uses the reasons of tzun-anchor/1 §10.1. Step 2 is the shape of §8.1 (exactly the nine members; leafIndex and anchorLeafIndex JSON integers in [0, 2^53 - 1]; publications a non-empty array: malformed_anchor), then both bodies (malformed_checkpoint), then both paths as arrays of 64-hex hashes (malformed_merkle_path). A log origin equal to the anchor origin fails step 2b (origin_not_in_domain). anchorPosition is present exactly when steps 1-5 hold and no publication is false. anchorNamespace is in every expect: 'test' whenever step 2's shape check holds and the anchor origin begins with test., whatever the verdict after it (§10.6: labelling yourself test is never an escalation), and otherwise null, since no case authenticates an origin. Step 6 dispatches each publication: an entry that is not an object is false (malformed_publication); an absent, non-string or unknown kind abstains (unsupported_publication_kind); an evm-calldata/1 entry in its envelope form carries no raw transaction and is not checked. Under §10.6 the reason for an undecided anchor is publication_not_checked when any publication was not checked, and otherwise the first publication's abstention. merkleProofValid is null when steps 4 and 5 did not run, and false when either failed. p is null until step 2 holds. expect.checks is the check catalogue of tzun-anchor/1 §10.7 as a report carries it ({ id, outcome, reason?, facts? }), in this order: anchor (the anchor as a whole: checked-correct when anchorValid is true, checked-wrong when false, otherwise abstain or not-checked as the reason is or is not an abstention of §10.1, with the anchor's reason; not-checked, absent, when nothing is attached); the six step checks anchor.spec, anchor.checkpoint, anchor.origin, anchor.leafIndex, anchor.inclusion, anchor.anchorInclusion (a step that fails is reported once, and each step after it is not-checked, blocked_by:<that step>; with nothing attached every step is not-checked, absent); then, once steps 1 to 5 hold, each publication in array order: anchor.publication[i] (the dispatch of §10.3 step 6), followed, only when it is checked-correct, by that kind's checks, each suffixed [i] (anchor.evm.tx[i] and anchor.evm.canonical[i]; a blocked_by names the suffixed id). Facts: anchor.origin, whenever it is checked-correct, carries originAuthenticated, namespace (the anchorNamespace) and chainChecked; anchor.leafIndex carries leafIndexChecked (true when a supplied sequence number was compared, whether or not it matched; false when none was supplied); no other check here carries facts.
format.c2spConforming: On every invalid body. true when the body is a conforming note text under C2SP tlog-checkpoint ("Note text") and signed-note v1.0.0, read literally: valid UTF-8 with no character below U+0020 other than LF; a final LF; at least three lines, none empty (the origin and any extension line MUST be non-empty); the size in ASCII decimal with no leading zero ("0" for the empty tree); the root the RFC 4648 section 4 base64 encoding, padded and with zero pad bits (RFC 4648 section 3.5), of a 32-byte RFC 6962 SHA-256 root, which at size 0 is the empty tree's, SHA-256(""). SHOULDs and NOT RECOMMENDEDs (spaces or "+" in the origin, extension lines) do not count. true means only a rule that Anchor §4.1 and §4.2 add to C2SP refuses the body.
format.stockParserAccepts: On every invalid body. true when github.com/transparency-dev/formats log.Checkpoint.Unmarshal at v0.1.1 returns no error for the body's UTF-8 bytes. It splits on LF into at most four parts and needs four (so at least three LFs); it requires a non-empty origin line and nothing else of it; it reads the size with strconv.ParseUint(size, 10, 64) (digits only, leading zeros allowed, at most 2^64 - 1) and the root with base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString (CR and LF skipped anywhere, padding required, unused bits ignored, no length check); anything after the third LF is returned as extension data. A gate running that parser must get exactly these flags, and must accept every body in bodies.valid with its origin, size and root.
